answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a stake in a scarce, costly-to-acquire resource, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to have double-voted or violated a signed task commitment. For example, agents may lock onyx-backed credits before joining a lagoon’s reputation-weighted auction; a lantern beacon can make the public audit trail easy to find, but it does not establish identity by itself. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up real capital in every fake account and risks losing it, making mass identities expensive rather than merely easy to create.
